title: A prescribed maximal split torus contains a defining parabolic cocharacter
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth, affine of finite type and geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after extension to an algebraic closure. Unipotent means admitting a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which all geometric points are unipotent matrices. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$, $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. A parabolic $k$-subgroup $P\subseteq G$ means a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose fppf right-coset sheaf $G/P$ is represented by a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here the coset sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras, and $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$. A minimal parabolic is one containing no strictly smaller parabolic $k$-subgroup; proper means $P\ne G$. Let $P\subseteq G$ be a parabolic $k$-subgroup, and let $S\subseteq P$ be a closed split torus maximal under inclusion among the closed split tori of $P$. There is a $k$-group homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to S$ such that, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, the subgroup $P(A)$ is exactly the set of $g\in G(A)$ for which the map $t\mapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$ extends from $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ to an $A$-morphism $\mathbf A^1_A\to G_A$. Here $\mathbf A^1_A=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$, and $\lambda$ is viewed in $G$ through $S\subseteq P\subseteq G$. The statement includes $P=G$, the trivial torus, and finite or imperfect $k$.

source.place: Theorem 25.1, printed p.544, converse and Galois averaging in a maximal torus of P; choose that torus through the prescribed S. The prescribed-torus choice is the preparatory assertion in the proof of Theorem 25.6(b), printed p.546, before the centralizer and semidirect-product conclusions. Only P=P(lambda) is asserted here, with no centralizer, Levi or conjugacy conclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-parabolic-containing-geometric-maximal-torus] to $D=S$ to obtain $S\subseteq T\subseteq P$ with $T$ geometrically maximal in $G$. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], choose a finite Galois extension $L/k$ splitting $T$: the continuous action on its finitely generated character group factors through a finite quotient. Write $\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-parabolic-root-sign-cone] over $L$ to $T_L\subseteq P_L\subseteq G_L$. It gives $\mu\in X_*(T_L)$ with $\Phi_P=\{\alpha:\langle\alpha,\mu\rangle\geq0\}$. Both $\Phi$ and $\Phi_P$ are $\Gamma$-stable: conjugation on the $k$-defined inclusion $\operatorname{Lie}(P)\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ permutes its character-weight spaces.

source.place: Theorem 25.1, p.544, Galois averaging and equation (166).

proof.text:
It remains to put $
u$ in the prescribed $S$. Since $T$ is commutative, define $f:S	imes\mathbf G_m	o T$ by $f(s,t)=s
u(t)$. On characters it gives $f^*:X^*(T)	o X^*(S	imes\mathbf G_m)\simeq\mathbf Z^{r+1}$, where $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Its image $N$ is a subgroup of a finite free abelian group, hence finite free by [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free]. Its Galois action is trivial, since it lies in the character group of the split source. Character antiduality therefore constructs a split torus $D_k(N)$ and a closed immersion $D_k(N)\hookrightarrow T$ from the surjection $X^*(T)	woheadrightarrow N$, through which $f$ factors. Restricting this factorization to the two factors shows that its image contains $S$ and $
u(\mathbf G_m)$ scheme-theoretically. It lies in $T\subseteq P$; maximality of the split torus $S$ forces $D_k(N)=S$ as closed subgroups. Hence $
u$ factors as a $k$-homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_m	o S$, and step 2 gives precisely the required equality $P(A)=P_\lambda(A)$ for every $A$. If $P=G$ the zero cocharacter already works; if $S$ is trivial this argument forces $
u=0$ and $P=G$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-b7aaf80a7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited node's statement, and Milne iAG2017 at printed p.544 (Thm 25.1 and eq. 166), p.546 (25.6(b): λ can be chosen in S), pp.453-455 (21.91-21.92) and p.379 (17.82-17.83). The item statement is true and matches 25.6(b); it is unchanged. Step 1: lem-sfb-parabolic-containing-geometric-maximal-torus gives S⊆T⊆P with T geometrically maximal, so T_L is a split maximal torus of G_L (elementary faithful-flatness argument). Antiduality gives a finite Galois splitting field L, and Φ_P is Γ-stable because Lie(P) is defined over k. Step 2: summing over Γ keeps the strict sign (every term is <0 for α∉Φ_P because Φ_P is exactly the ≥0 set), so ν_L∈C(P_L,T_L). The root-sign iff and the field-extension clause of lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry give P_L=P_{ν_L}, and the ideal equality descends by faithful flatness. Step 3: N=im f* is Galois-trivial and free (Mathlib leaf). The antiduality closed-immersion criterion gives a split torus D_k(N) with S⊆D_k(N)⊆T⊆P, so maximality of S puts ν in S. This argument avoids the rational conjugacy of maximal split tori, which would be circular. New nodes: both are true (Milne 17.82/17.10; 21.91-21.92 and (166)). Both are statement-only, self-contained and strictly smaller than the item. I tested them on GL_2 with the Borel (a>b), P=G, a torus, and anisotropic SL_1(H)/R. Duplicate search over about 11 sfb candidates found none. No cycle. No off-unit route; no SGA. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons (scalar extension of exterior powers and duals) and lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change (Mathlib leaf) are generic tools, neither the trace formula, Poincaré duality, nor a step of their proofs, so I accept both. No fixes.
